plastic.title: Plastic Waste
actions: Separate the plastic item from other waste.
Empty and rinse the container when appropriate.
Check the resin identification code and local recycling guidelines.
plastic.warning: The Plastic class alone cannot identify the exact resin type, such as PET or HDPE, or guarantee local recyclability.

paper.title: Paper Waste
actions: Keep paper clean and dry.
Separate paper contaminated with food, oil, or other substances.
Check which paper types are accepted by your local recycling facility.
paper.warning: Wet or heavily contaminated paper may not be suitable for recycling.

cardboard.title: Cardboard Waste
actions: Flatten cardboard boxes to reduce storage and transportation space.
Remove food residue and non-paper components when possible.
Take the cardboard to a collection point that accepts it.
cardboard.warning: Grease-contaminated cardboard may not be accepted for recycling.

glass.title: Glass Waste
actions: Separate glass items from other waste.
Empty containers safely when appropriate.
Use a designated glass collection bin if available.
glass.warning: Never handle broken glass with bare hands. Follow local safety guidelines.

metal.title: Metal Waste
actions: Separate metal items from other waste.
Empty and clean containers when appropriate.
Check whether your local recycling facility accepts the specific metal.
metal.warning: Do not handle pressurized containers or containers holding hazardous substances.

battery.title: Used Battery
actions: Keep the battery separate from ordinary household waste.
Find a designated battery collection or recycling point.
Follow the collection facility's instructions for safe handling and transport.
battery.warning: Do not puncture, burn, or place batteries in ordinary recycling bins. Damaged batteries may require special handling.

biological.title: Organic Waste
actions: Separate food scraps and other organic waste from recyclable materials.
Check whether a local composting program is available.
Follow local guidelines for acceptable compostable materials.
biological.warning: Not all organic waste is suitable for every composting system.

clothes.title: Used Clothing
actions: Donate or reuse clothing that is still in good condition.
Separate damaged textiles and look for textile recycling programs.
Check the collection program's accepted materials.
clothes.warning: Not all textiles can be recycled through standard collection programs.

shoes.title: Used Shoes
actions: Donate or reuse shoes that are still wearable.
Look for collection programs that accept used footwear.
Check whether the program accepts damaged shoes and mixed materials.
shoes.warning: Recycling options depend on the shoe's materials and the receiving facility.

trash.title: Unclassified or Mixed Waste
actions: Inspect the item for material labels or recycling symbols.
Identify its material before deciding how to dispose of it.
Follow local waste disposal guidelines if the material cannot be identified.
trash.warning: The Trash prediction does not necessarily mean the item is non-recyclable. Further inspection may be needed.
